configuration: verification/seaice_itd/input: the 80x42 channel with the multi-category ice thickness distribution (SEAICE_ITD, 7 categories, linear remapping between categories, Thorndike ridging with SEAICE_cf=2 setting the ice strength, useHibler79IceStrength off), LSR solver at LSR_ERROR=1e-12, multidimensional advection scheme 77 of every category, ocean frozen; 48 steps of 1800 s (one day) instead of the deck's 12. Graded: every <field>.<final iteration>.data written by the end-of-run state dump (ocean U, V, W, T, S, Eta, PH, PHL; sea-ice UICE, VICE and the thickness, area, snow and enthalpy fields of the thermodynamics in use), read with the shape and precision of the .meta sidecar; the initial-state dump and STDOUT are not graded.
variant: ic/variant is ic/nominal with SEAICE_cf=2.0000000000000004 in data.seaice instead of 2, replacing the deck's own line: one ulp (2.2e-16 relative) on the ice-strength parameter, verified to be a distinct double. It enters every viscosity and stress evaluation of the dynamics, so the two runs differ at round-off level from the first step without leaving the round-off floor; the recorded spread is the check's real sensitivity under this rule.

comparison.files: every <field>.<iteration>.data at the final iteration of the reference, minus not_graded; the candidate must have the same set at the same iteration
comparison.format: raw big-endian IEEE floating point as written by pkg/mdsio (writeBinaryPrec=64), precision and dimensions from the .meta sidecar

evidence.floor_how: worst relative difference over all graded fields (in FV) between the optimised gfortran build (linux_amd64_gfortran optfile, -O3) and the IEEE build of the same source (genmake2 -ieee, -O0 -ffloat-store) on the nominal deck, run natively on the x86_64 host on 2026-09-02; the two builds pass each other under this rule

faults.how: same build and deck as the reference with one parameter changed, compared under this rule, natively on the x86_64 host on 2026-09-02

warrant: The observable is every cell of every prognostic field in the final state dump, compared as |c - r| <= 1e-10 + 1e-08|r|. The relative part is the working bound: the graded fields span ten orders of magnitude (ice area of order one, velocities of order 1e-2 m/s, ice enthalpies of order 1e5 J/kg, ocean temperature of order 10), so a single absolute number would be either unreachable for the enthalpies or vacuous for the velocities; the absolute part only covers cells whose reference value is at or near zero. The bound is physical because the dynamics is an iterative viscous-plastic solve whose converged answer is fixed by the rheology: a dropped term in the stress divergence, a wrong viscosity regularisation, a cheaper solver stopped early, or a single-precision state moves the ice velocity by parts in 1e-6 or more within a few steps, far above 1e-10. It is achievable because the source path under test (seaice_itd_remap.F and seaice_itd_redist.F (category remapping), seaice_do_ridging.F and seaice_calc_ice_strength.F (ridging scheme and strength), seaice_growth.F per category, seaice_advdiff.F once per category field, and seaice_lsr.F) is deterministic in a single process with tiles swept in fixed order (GLOBAL_SUM_ORDER_TILES), so two correct runs differ only by round-off amplified through the solver iterations; the nominal-versus-variant spread recorded by selfcheck is the measurement of that amplification under this exact rule, and the bound is finalised against it with the human. The window is short (one to two simulated days, 48 steps) so round-off has no time to grow.
